title: Samach Vav Part 233:
blurb: Samach Vav p. 190-191: This explains why "when the Temple is not standing, a person’s table affects atonement": The table, like the altar, offers and refines the animal soul, drawing down from the world of tohu and thereby bringing atonement. Thus a meal is like prayer in the fact that it refines the animal soul, as well as the physical elements of mineral, vegetable and animal that are consumed in a meal. This refinement of the animal soul is also achieved through our work: You refine your corner of the physical world and the animal soul when you run your business faithfully and ethically, without any deceit, as well as not allowing yourself to be overconsumed with your job, which then disturbs your ability to study Torah and pray. Especially when you do your work for the sake of heaven, intending to do a mitzvah -- give charity and study Torah in peace. Because, left on its own, the animal soul is driven by self-interest and will not hesitate to lie or steal for personal gain. As such, when a person refrains from acting unfaithfully, he is refining his animal soul. Elsewhere it is explained that prayer refines the cognitive soul -- the intelligence of the animal soul. But the refinement of the animal soul itself -- its emotions -- is through eating a meal. Yet prayer also refines the emotions; the difference is that in prayer the refinement is potential, while at a meal it is actualized.
